summary: setup.py contains a dropper-shaped harness that bash-executes a sibling setup.sh at install time; payload file not shipped in this version
details: setup.py defines execute_deployer(), which checks for a sibling setup.sh, chmods it 0755, and invokes it via subprocess.run(["bash", SCRIPT_PATH], check=True) as part of the install flow. In this sdist the setup.sh file is not present (absent from SOURCES.txt and the extracted tree), so no shell payload is executed during pip install of 1.2.1. The package ships with an empty README and a generic 'Cloud Run Deployer' framing, and the install harness is structurally a dropper: any future release, patched sdist, or locally-added setup.sh would be executed at install time with the installer's privileges. No credential reads, no outbound network, and no other malicious behavior are present in the current artifact.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
